title: Peeping into the 25 Club to hear Joe Oliver as a boy
summary: As a youngster he climbed on a beer barrel to listen at the window of the 25 club on Franklin Street, where Joe Oliver played, until the police chased him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh, man. Now that's a fella I could play a home. I remember one night I wasn't playing yet. I was just a youngster getting around, you know. And I was standing, he was playing with a big tall fella, who plays violin. I don't know where did he get that tone out of that violin, but did he have some tone? Sweat say it was an electric violin.
It was electric? No, it wasn't.
I swear to say it was.

It was. You could be on the outside like I was listening. Yeah, it was a while. I climbed on top of a beer barrel and I was in the window looking in, you see. Yeah. There were a lot of youngsters in the district then.
On Franklin between Iberville and Canal.
25, that's right. Big 25. And they had a fella by the name. I heard my brother, this fella, tell me his name was Valtu.
Oh, yeah. I've heard that. Professor Vanetta talks about him a lot.

Yeah? Yeah. An old man Valtu. Yeah. Well, I'm telling you. He's down here. That's the one I heard. I was in that one they had Joe Oliver, that old man Valtu. I think they had about five pieces in there. Drums and whatever else they had. I don't know. Because I was peeping in that window like a transom I was looking. I was looking. I stand on top of a beer bell and something else. And the police had come and cracked me.
And I mean I hopped off that thing too quick for a hurry. Yeah.
There's a lot of youngsters around there then, you see. It's a shame.
All you wanted to do was listen to the music then.

That's all. It's a shame. Couldn't it help? Yeah. I was trying to make my wealth, you see. Mm-hmm. And, but there was such a bunch of fellas that looked like they wasn't interested. All they were interested in making that money and that's all. Nothing else behind them. Yeah. Yeah. And so, fool with them kind of guys, I never would get nowhere. And I guess in a band over the river, Red Allen's daddy. Oh yeah. In the brass band. They didn't have ballrooms too much then. They had them little hole in the wall, you know. Yeah. I don't guess I should be talking about it over the river.
